correctness.rationale: The line-graph cluster equivalence forces root components to be stars or triangles. The proof checks every possible one-edge addition, excluding 2-edge stars and all unused-base-vertex configurations except one isolated vertex with triangles. Each admissible labeled root-component partition is unique; the exponential formula and spectrum arguments are exact. Exhaustive direct induced-subgraph tests for n=3..7 agree with the independent recurrence on 545 maximal subsets and 2,131,016 total examined subsets. Unbounded n is handled by proof, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: Cluster vertex deletion is a motivated hereditary graph modification problem; the finding describes every facet of the cluster-inducing complex on a classical Johnson graph, gives a closed cardinality EGF and exact size spectrum, and identifies the exceptional pure order n=5. The distinction between triangle components, 2-edge stars, and the isolated-vertex exception is structurally necessary and not an arbitrary parameter substitution. It supplies more than minimum cardinality or routine finite enumeration.
